correctness.rationale: The Gaussian complex-exponential identity proves equality of every integer moment, while signed-Laplace uniqueness and positive-axis analyticity give distinct transforms with isolated crossings. The pressure reduction gives a strictly concave unique terminal root, strictly monotone in the seed; complete derivative-jet equality follows by ODE differentiation and nonanalyticity by factorial growth. At baseline pressure 1/2, Gaussian symmetry, 18 interval lower sums >0.1979 and a Mills tail bound <0.0864 rigorously give -H(1/2)>0.1115; a derivative bound gives attack gap >0.16056. The standalone checker verifies the finite strict numeric margins. Scope: deterministic constant-rate closed heterogeneous SIR with positive infection seed.

value.rationale: The finite-support all-moment identifiability intuition fails sharply for unbounded susceptibility even when every initial time derivative matches. The explicit epidemic construction proves >16 percentage points of attack-size difference with identical rates, seeds and all susceptibility moments, and the generic-seed theorem shows the discrepancy is not a uniquely tuned artifact. This directly limits moment-based forecasting and Taylor-jet extrapolation; not a bare renaming, toy isolated numerical sample, or assertion about full-trajectory inference.
